captions.linkedin:
Most quants chase stock momentum. They're hunting the wrong target. 📊

Ehsani and Linnainmaa (2022, Journal of Finance) made the cleaner argument: it isn't stocks that have momentum, it's factors. And factor momentum quietly subsumes stock, industry, and intermediate momentum as special cases of the same thing.

The mechanism is simple. Anomaly factors are autocorrelated. A factor that beat its mean over the last 12 months tends to do it again next month.

Here's the complete logic. No black box:

🔹 FACTOR LIBRARY, 20-50 long/short anomaly factors.
🔹 TRAILING 12M, rank factors by prior-year return.
🔹 SIGN ORIENT, flip negative-return factors to short.
🔹 EQUAL RISK, weight across factors to avoid vol concentration.
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE, refresh signs and hold 1 month.

If you already run a multi-factor book, factor momentum is a meta-layer that times your own exposures. You stop fighting sleeves when they're down and lean in when they're up.

The paper's headline result: average factor return is 6 bps after a down year vs 51 bps after an up year. The autocorrelation is real.
